stories.title: Suparco warns of worsening smog across Punjab
summary: According to Suparco’s smog assessment for Nov 17, satellite observations recorded 386 active fire detections in Punjab and 304 in the transboundary region during the preceding 24 hours.
The satellite-based monitoring is intended to track the geographical spread of smog, identify fire hotspots and provide an assessment of atmospheric conditions across Punjab.

The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) also forecast fog and smog at isolated places in Lahore, Sialkot, Narowal, Sheikhupura, Okara, Kasur, Faisalabad, Jhang, Khanewal, Multan and surrounding areas during morning and night over the next 48 hours.

stories.title: Israel forces kill 3 Palestinians in fresh Gaza push
summary: An October 2025 ceasefire halted major fighting in the Israel-Gaza war but has not stopped Israeli attacks in Gaza.

Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops. “Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas’ agreement to the roadmap to the test,” the report said.

Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as “pure disinformation”, accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to continue its aggression in Gaza.

stories.title: PTI’s legal eagles ‘shake and make up’
summary: Earlier, Mr Raja had acknowledged differences with Mr Khosa and Salman Safdar after their meeting with Imran Khan, amid speculation that the PTI founder wanted major changes within the party.

Advocate Khalid Yousuf Chaudhry told Dawn that the PTI had learnt through the media that the jail administration had taken Imran Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for treatment. “It is nothing but contempt of the Supreme Court.
On Jan 17, 2025, an accountability court in Islamabad sentenced Imran Khan to 14 years in prison and Bushra Bibi to seven years in the case.

stories.title: Pakistan's mango exports fall 36pc amid US-Iran war: exporters' association
summary: According to All Pakistan Fruit and Vegetables Exporters Association, the country exported 78,000 tonnes of mangoes this year, compared with 123,000 tons last year.
Exports to the Middle East, a major market for Pakistani mangoes, dropped from 36,000 tonnes last year to 14,500 tonnes this year, the association said.
Climate change has reduced Pakistan’s total mango production by 35pc, according to the association.

stories.title: ‘Have the courage to listen to the debate you started’: Bilawal sticks to his guns after speaking his ‘truth’
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Wednesday maintained that his recent remarks on the country’s political situation were the “truth”, urging government representatives to have the “courage” to listen to his point of view.

Speaking in an interview on Hum News programme ‘Faisla Aap Ka’, Bilawal reiterated his stance from his Tuesday’s speech, cautioning against new provinces and calling for a “political reset” so public issues could be addressed.

Responding to a query about reserved seats on Geo News, Bilawal emphasised that his suggestion was “in the context of a political, democratic reset that could restore the trust of the opposition parties”.

stories.title: PTA says submarine cable fault may cause internet connectivity issues
summary: In the meantime, the authority said internet traffic was “being rerouted through alternative international links to minimise the impact and ensure service continuity to the greatest extent possible”.

Internet monitor NetBlocks confirmed later that a decline in internet connectivity was causing slow service. “The incident is consistent with a fault on the SMW5 international subsea cable system with operators now attempting to establish alternative routes,” it said.
On July 1, a fault in the SMW5 international submarine cable system caused widespread connectivity issues in Pakistan.

stories.title: KP governor forms 8-member commission to probe illegal placer gold mining
summary: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Wednesday constituted an eight-member inquiry commission to probe illegal placer gold mining in the province.

According to the notification, the commission will inquire into the extent, history and nature of illegal placer gold mining in KP, particularly in Kohat, Nowshera, Karak and other affected districts.

The probe has been set up in the aftermath of an attack that led to the martyrdom of 10 police personnel in the Gumbat area of Kohat district on Nov 11 while they were returning from an operation against illegal placer gold mining along the Indus River.

stories.title: 'SME financing targeted at Rs2tr by 2028'
summary: He emphasised the need to move beyond conventional, collateral-based lending towards technology-enabled, data-driven and inclusive financing solutions, supported by stronger participation from banks, fintech companies, development finance institutions and private investors.

He highlighted the potential for engagement with Singapore's financial technology ecosystem through the Global Finance & Technology Network (GFTN), calling for greater mobilisation of private capital through risk-sharing arrangements and blended finance.

The minister also visited the Singapore FinTech Festival, inaugurating Ignite's Pakistan Pavilion and interacting with companies including Tax Nerd Pakistan, Ping Up, Bagh-e, Fortanixor Technologies, and Lendverse/Tawha Technologies.

stories.title: Thar coal mining to shift to national grid
summary: Work has formally begun on shifting Thar coal mining from diesel to the national grid, which will save Pakistan around $25 million to $30 million in foreign exchange every year.
Power for mining operations, which costs around 33 cents per kilowatt-hour when generated from diesel, will drop to 13 cents, a reduction of over 60%.

Carbon emissions are expected to fall by about 80,000 tonnes a year and diesel-powered mining vehicles will be progressively converted into electric systems, supporting long-term decarbonisation goals.

stories.title: Govt drafts marble policy to curb wastage
summary: Advisor to the Prime Minister for Industries Haroon Akhtar Khan chaired a meeting with Marble Association representatives to discuss a policy to make the sector globally competitive, the Ministry of Industries said on Wednesday.
The government is developing the Marble Policy 2026-29 to modernise the industry through advanced technology and value addition, covering the value chain from quarrying to exports.
He said sustainable access to raw materials and processing technologies were essential for strengthening the sector and improving the quality of Pakistani marble in international markets.

stories.title: PSX slides 1,223 points over political noise
summary: It put considerable pressure on heavyweight stocks from sectors such as cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration, oil marketing, power generation and refineries.
Sector-wise, banks, cement and oil & gas remained under pressure, whereas fertiliser and refineries showed some resilience.
He said the index was likely to remain volatile amid geopolitical uncertainty, oil price fluctuations and domestic political developments.

stories.title: Delegation expected to visit Brazil in Jan
summary: He emphasised that cooperation with Brazil would help Pakistan improve agricultural productivity, strengthen food security and enhance the international competitiveness of its farm products.
He stated that Pakistani agricultural and livestock experts would visit Brazil to study its advanced farming practices, research institutions and livestock development models.
Both sides agreed to promote institutional collaboration between the Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC) and Embrapa.

stories.title: ICJ report sees 'judicial capture' in Pakistan after 26th, 27th Constitutional Amendments
summary: A report released by the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) on Wednesday said that the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments led to a “systemic judicial capture” in Pakistan.

The 26th Amendment, passed in October 2024, carved constitutional benches out of the Supreme Court, with their members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority.
On Wednesday, the ICJ released a report — titled ‘Judicial Capture: Independence of the Judiciary in Pakistan after the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments’.

stories.title: US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
summary: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph.
Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on Jan 3, when he would become the first Black politician to hold the powerful post.

Jeffries’s nomination contrasts with a more competitive leadership contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran party chief Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen.

stories.title: Pakistan conducts successful launch of Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile: ISPR
summary: The Pakistan Army on Wednesday successfully launched the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, according to the military’s media wing.

It added that the missile would “significantly enhance the operational flexibility and strike range of the Pakistan Army’s Rocket Force Command, further strengthening the country’s overall conventional deterrence and defence posture”.

According to the interior ministry, he said that the launch represented a “significant advancement in the defence sector”. “The successful test of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile marks a major milestone in the country’s defence capabilities,” Naqvi said.

stories.title: Nawaz hails his govt’s ‘serious’ work on AJK development as PML-N charts 100-day plan
summary: The PML-N said its top leadership, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, discussed development and reconstruction in AJK with the region’s president and premier, both of whom belong to the PML-N.
PM Shehbaz, AJK PM Gillani and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also addressed the meeting, with their remarks live-streamed on state media.
She said the Punjab government was ready to help in AJK’s development if needed.

stories.title: ICJ report deplores judicial independence in Pakistan after 26th, 27th Constitutional Amendments
summary: A report released by the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) on Wednesday deplored the state of judicial independence in Pakistan after the passage of the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments.
The amendment also introduced key changes to the judicial appointment process, specifically in Article 175-A.

The erosion of judicial independence was not done through the overt removal of judges as was done during military rule, most recently by General Musharraf,119 but through constitutional amendments adopted by Parliament," it added.

stories.title: 'He who claims equity must come with clean hands': Asif hits back at Bilawal
summary: You took credit for the entire amendment, and today you’re saying that votes were cast forcibly.” Chaudhry claimed Bilawal and his party opposed creation of new provinces in order to maintain control over resources.
So when did you start fearing the vote?” Chaudhry said. “During 17 years of [PPP] rule, your governance has drained the blood of the people of Sindh.

The JI chief further stated that the PPP chairman should recall his party’s role in the ethnic unrest triggered by the 1972 language bill in Sindh before warning of bloodshed over the creation of new provinces.

stories.title: 'It set a positive tone': Xi's airport greeting for Trump breaks decades-long precedent
summary: Xi Jinping’s personal welcome to US President Donald Trump at Shenzhen airport on Wednesday for a summit made him China’s first paramount leader in decades to greet a foreign counterpart on arrival.

But Trump’s personal welcome is believed to be the first by a paramount leader in China in decades — and marks an upgrade to his high-profile summit trip to Beijing in May, when Vice President Han Zheng was there to meet him.

Xi told Trump on the tarmac on Wednesday that during his state visit to the United States, the “presidential couple came to the airport in person and hosted a grand welcome ceremony”, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.

stories.title: Untenable stalemate
summary: NEARLY nine months into a conflict of choice that has rattled economies from Europe to Asia, there seem to be few agreeable options for the US where ending the Iran war is concerned.
The Iranian foreign minister was also in Islamabad for the event, and praised Pakistan’s efforts to broker peace.
The collective voice from the states of this region is clearly against war, while the majority of the American people also appear uninterested in fresh clashes with Iran.

stories.title: 15,000-tonne LPG cargo arrives from Abu Dhabi under new policy to ease shortages
summary: In a statement, the Petroleum Division said that SSGC LPG Limited (SSL) – a subsidiary of the state-run Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (SSGCL) – had imported a record 15,000 metric tonnes of LPG cargo, the largest of its kind that berthed at Engro Vopak Terminal Limited (EVTL).
Under the cabinet decision, the government also directed state-owned companies to lead LPG imports and strengthen the country’s supply chain, especially in winter.
The SOEs — PSO, Pakistan LNG Ltd, SSL and Parco-LPG — have been engaged with various suppliers from Saudi Arabia and Oman for LPG supply.

stories.title: £190m corruption case: IHC directs proper medical care, hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi as per prison rules
summary: On January 17, 2025, an accountability court in Islamabad sentenced Imran to 14 years in prison and Bushra to seven years in the case.

During the proceedings, the court also took up a fresh miscellaneous application filed on behalf of Bushra, raising concerns about her deteriorating eyesight, need for surgery, possible post-operative complications and the medical facilities available to her in prison.
On Nov 11, 2026, Barrister Safdar and Khosa also met Imran and Bushra at Adiala jail for nearly three hours, following IHC orders.

stories.title: UN nuclear watchdog says US-Saudi nuclear agreement 'satisfactory'
summary: UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi on Wednesday welcomed a deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia on equipping the kingdom with a civilian nuclear programme.

The deal announced in July has provoked questions about the risks of nuclear proliferation. “It’s a very satisfactory outcome that we have with this agreement,” Grossi told reporters after opening an International Atomic Energy Agency board of governors’ meeting.

In his opening statement, Grossi told the board that the US and Saudi Arabia in October requested the IAEA “to take the necessary steps to implement safeguards and verification measures” for their agreement.

stories.title: Pakistan tighten grip on second Test as Sri Lanka stumble to 74-3
summary: Pakistan strengthened their grip on the second Test on Wednesday, taking a commanding 227-run first-innings lead before reducing Sri Lanka to 74-3 at stumps on the second day at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.

After wicket-keeper-batter Ghazi Ghori’s half-century and an explosive contribution from Razaullah helped Pakistan reach 325 all out, the hosts’ fast bowlers struck repeatedly to leave Sri Lanka facing a daunting task on day three.
Kumara was Sri Lanka’s most effective bowler, removing Azan, Pakistan captain Babar Azam (eight), Saqib and Saud Shakeel (24) to put the visitors in a strong position.

stories.title: 'You want Karachi to exploit it': Hafiz Naeem blasts Bilawal for using 'ethnic tensions' to retain power
summary: Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeem ur Rehman on Wednesday accused Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari of "exploiting" Karachi, while alleging that the PPP used ethnic tensions between Sindhis and Muhajirs to create fear and retain political power.
"That is why the people of Karachi resent the PPP.

You have occupied the city through an imposed arrangement." He added that the politics of the PPP and MQM would no longer be accepted in Karachi and Larkana, calling for "political accountability and merit-based governance".

stories.title: Petrol and high-speed diesel drop by Rs3 per litre
summary: On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.

stories.title: Woman killed as high-voltage cable falls on house in Balochistan's Turbat
summary: GWADAR: A woman was killed, while her husband and son sustained critical burn injuries after an 11,000-volt power line snapped and fell on their house in the Wasto Bazaar area of Turbat in the early hours of Wednesday.
The high-tension wire fell on the residence, electrocuting and severely burning the family members, who were rushed to the Teaching Hospital Turbat, hospital officials said.
Earlier this month, three members of a single family were electrocuted to death when a high-voltage transmission line above their house snapped and fell on them in Punjab’s Bahawalnagar.

stories.title: 'Come to your senses': Bilawal advises govt to 'calm down' and hold a 'debate you started' on provinces
summary: The remarks come after Defence Minister Khawaja Asif hit back at Bilawal earlier in the day over his criticism of the government and calls for a "political reset", questioning his moral standing to lecture others while pointing to the PPP's 18-year rule in Sindh.

A day earlier, Bilawal had called for a "political reset' to restore public confidence in state institutions, urging the government to revive dialogue with opposition parties, including the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), and end political victimisation.

Bilawal further asked that if provinces were to be divided, "does that mean only the PCB has the right to speak on the matter while I should remain silent and go home?" While defending his earlier statement, he said: "Did I ask people to come out and protest or to resist?

stories.title: Pakistan takes pride in safeguarding its invaluable Gandhara heritage: culture minister
summary: Foreign Secretary Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad welcomed the international delegates and Buddhist monastics, highlighting Gandhara's significance as a shared heritage of humanity and a bridge between civilisations.
The monastics also highlighted the importance of recognising Gandhara as a shared heritage and improving facilities for Buddhist pilgrims, scholars and religious visitors.
During the event, Curator Elli Takagaki unveiled Colours of Pakistan: Gandhara Edition, a publication showcasing Gandharan heritage sites, Buddhist monastics and international engagement.

stories.title: Analysis: Big Three converge in Shenzhen for 'mini Yalta'
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping will host his US and Russian counterparts for an unprecedented trilateral meeting today (Thursday), on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in the southeastern city of Shenzhen.

In Beijing, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Presidents Xi, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin would have an in-depth exchange of views on global peace, calling the summit one of “groundbreaking significance”.

The Chinese and Russian leaders, he adds, are also sceptical of Trump’s ability to deliver on his promises. “Not much should be expected from the Shenzhen meeting beyond diplomatic optics; substance is likely to remain elusive,” he says.

stories.title: ASEAN sec gen to visit Pakistan for first time in over two decades from Nov 18 to 20: FO
summary: Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Secretary General Dr Kao Kim Hourn will undertake a working visit to Pakistan from November 18 to 20 at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday.
The statement added that the visit underscored the "shared commitment of Pakistan and ASEAN to deepening and diversifying their cooperation".
Earlier this year, FM Dar reaffirmed full support to ASEAN's continued efforts to promote regional peace, stability, prosperity and sustainable development.

stories.title: Indian Air Force’s Rafale fleet down to 32, aviation publication says, backing Pakistan’s claim of downing four jets
summary: The Indian Air Force (IAF) has 32 French-made Rafale fighter jets in service, down from 36 before the May 2025 conflict with Pakistan, according to estimates published by British aviation magazine Flight International.
In the immediate aftermath of the conflict, Pakistan said it shot down at least six Indian fighter jets during the conflict, including the French-made Rafale.
At the time, a high-ranking French intelligence official had also confirmed to CNN that one Rafale fighter jet operated by the IAF was downed by Pakistan.

stories.title: Pakistan set to send first astronaut to China’s Tiangong Space Station through Shenzhou-24 mission: SUPARCO
summary: According to a SUPARCO spokesperson, the Pakistani astronaut would serve as a payload specialist, marking the country’s first participation in a crewed mission to China’s space station.
Read: Pakistan nears historic first astronaut mission Meanwhile, the Chinese space agency has unveiled the official logo of the Shenzhou-24 mission, featuring jasmine, Pakistan’s national flower.

China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship will be launched in the near future, with a Pakistani astronaut joining the mission as a payload specialist in China's first manned space mission to include a foreign astronaut.

stories.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel and Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
summary: The body overseeing US President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza war ​accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ‌ceasefire in danger of collapse.
Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops.
The Board of Peace was established ​by Trump to oversee ⁠his ambitious plan to end the war that Israel launched in response to Hamas-led attacks from Gaza in October 2023.

Sheikhupura recorded 172 anomalies, of which 154 had been attended to and extinguished, while 18 remained pending.
Of these, 13 had been attended to, while seven remained pending, giving a response rate of 65pc.

stories.title: Pakistan, Turkiye discuss expanding defence cooperation in electronic warfare, drone and aerospace technologies
summary: ACM Sidhu also assured the visiting dignitary of the PAF’s all-out support in the areas of pilot training, professional development and capacity-building endeavours of the Turkish Air Force, the statement added.

Both air chiefs identified “substantial opportunities” for enhancing bilateral defence cooperation in unmanned and autonomous systems, electronic warfare, advanced aerospace technologies, and indigenous research, development and production.
Earlier in May, the PAF and Turkish Air Force reaffirmed their “growing strategic convergence” in defence, aerospace innovation and emerging technologies during ACM Sidhu’s official visit to Turkiye.

stories.title: Military successfully tests launch of Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile
summary: Pakistan successfully test-fired the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, marking another “significant milestone” in the country's efforts to strengthen its defence capabilities, the military's media wing said on Wednesday.
Pakistan Army today conducted a successful launch of Fatah-3 Supersonic Cruise Missile, marking another significant milestone in the advancement of national defence capabilities, according to ISPR.
The successful test of the Fatah-III supersonic missile is a major advance in the defence sector," said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on X.
